description:
Advances: ancora.derive

Severity: Medium (calibrated). Consolidated findings F9, F13, F17 — the three tracked items that are genuine decisions rather than fixes. Each needs a call before any code moves, which is why none of them could land on the ship branch.

F9 — THE ETS MEMO IS DEAD CODE AND THE SPEC SAYS OTHERWISE. Six of nine reviewers found this independently, chasing four different symptoms; it was the single most-agreed finding in the review. RunContext creates a public ETS table on every gate run and deletes it without a single write. memo_put/4, memo_get/2 and the kind-rank arbitration table have ZERO callers in lib/ — the only callers are six assertions in test/ancora/git_test.exs. Gate.def_indexes/2 and Derive.resolve_file/4 never receive the RunContext, so they could not consult it even if they wanted to. Meanwhile requirement ancora.derive.memo_is_run_scoped states that parsed ASTs, DefIndex results and resolver results are memoized there. Roughly 60 lines make every reader believe caching exists.
The decision: DELETE or IMPLEMENT. Deleting requires narrowing a must in memo_is_run_scoped, which trips append/must_downgraded and needs its own ADR. Implementing requires a bench run first — and note the performance work measured 122 of 247 Code.string_to_quoted calls in a real run as re-parses of a file an earlier stage already parsed, so a working memo has real value. Sequence this with the per-binding rework child, which shares the call path. The batch-port half of the same struct is live and spec-earned; only the memo half is dead.

F13 — spec-exceptions is a fifth spec block type that is parsed, schema-validated, counted, and returned on the semver-stable parse_file/2 map, while NO requirement mentions it and nothing ever reads it. Removing the key from a published return map is a compatibility break; naming it in the grammar means giving Ancora.Verifier something to do with its covers field. Either direction is a release-scoped decision.

F17 — Ancora.Review extracts bindings with a REGEX while the AST resolver sits one module away. Swapping the extractor changes which bindings appear on watched-interface cards, so the correct contract has to be written into ancora.review first (see the artifact-size sibling ticket), and only then does this become a testable change against it.

Sequencing: ready now, no blockers. F17 moved to ancora-gqb by ruling (2026-09-03). F9 ruled DELETE, so this ticket no longer blocks ancora-xla.3. Scope is F9 (delete the memo half, narrow the must under an ADR) and F13 (deprecate spec-exceptions) only.

Ruling needed before code moves (Manuel): (F9) delete the dead ETS memo and narrow ancora.derive.memo_is_run_scoped under an ADR, or implement the memo so the must becomes true? (F13) name spec-exceptions in the grammar and give Verifier something to do with covers, or schedule the key for removal in the next major? (F17) once gqb's contract line exists, swap Ancora.Review's regex binding extractor for the AST resolver?
Recommended default from the ticket: F9 implement, because xla.3 measured 122 of 247 string_to_quoted calls as re-parses, so a working run-scoped memo has value and keeps the must honest; thread RunContext into def_indexes/2 and resolve_file/4. F13 schedule removal: document the key as deprecated in the parse_file/2 contract now, remove in 2.0. F17 yes, swap, tested against gqb's contract line.
Worker: if no comment on this ticket records a ruling when you start, park and ask. Do not choose on Manuel's behalf and do not implement more than one option.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests under ancora.derive (test/ancora/git_test.exs memo assertions become production-path tests, test/ancora/derive/pipeline_test.exs), ancora.parsing (test/ancora/parser_test.exs, test/ancora/schema_test.exs for spec-exceptions), ancora.review (test/ancora/review_test.exs watched-card bindings from the AST resolver)
- Behaviors to demonstrate: per ruling. If implement: memo_put/memo_get have callers in lib/, a second parse of the same blob in one run is a memo hit asserted by counter, and the table is still deleted at run end. If delete: the memo half of RunContext is gone, memo_is_run_scoped is narrowed with an ADR in the same diff, and the batch-port half is untouched. F13: the parse_file/2 return contract states the key's status. F17: watched-card bindings come from the resolver and match the contract line gqb wrote
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: memo_is_run_scoped describes what the code does, spec-exceptions has a stated status on the public parse map, and the review extractor matches its written contract.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/derive/run_context.ex (delete the memo half only; the batch-port half stays), lib/ancora/derive.ex (dead memo references only)
- lib/ancora/parser.ex, lib/ancora/schema.ex, lib/ancora/schema/exception.ex, lib/ancora/verifier.ex
- test/ancora/**, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.parsing.spec.md (substantive)
- .spec/decisions/** (ADR if a must is narrowed)
- docs/migration.md, README.md (deprecation note for F13)

- Any .spec/specs/<subject>.spec.md that `mix spec.check --base <your base>` names in a derived/drift, derived/growth or derived/shrink finding caused by THIS ticket's own diff (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator after the fifth admission defect of this epic. Derivation is file-scoped: every production function called anywhere in a test file joins every subject tagged anywhere in that file, and siblings merging into the epic tip change that set under you, so no list written at admission stays correct. Rule: acknowledgment edits only. Write one substantive requirement or scenario statement describing what THIS ticket changed as THAT subject observes it, verified by execution that the named input actually reaches that subject. Never restate another subject's contract in a second home, never weaken a must, never delete a requirement, never use a Spec-Ack trailer for it. If the subject genuinely observes no change from your work, say so in your completion record and stop; that is an escalation to the orchestrator, not a failure. Every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; an affects: entry on your own ADR is the expected form.)
- Any spec whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false, for the sole purpose of correcting that statement in the same diff. Recorded after ancora-v1n shipped a corpus holding two scenarios that predicted opposite outcomes from identical input, because the spec stating the old rule was withheld from its Allowed list and the worker retagged around the conflict instead of flagging it. If you find a requirement anywhere in .spec/ that your change falsifies, fixing it here is in scope and expected. Say so in your completion record.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/review/** (F17 moved to ancora-gqb)
- lib/mix/tasks/**
- lib/ancora/output*
- lib/ancora/git/**

Out of Scope (intent):
- no removal of the spec-exceptions key from the published 1.x return map
- no base-tree narrowing or MapSet hoist (ancora-xla.3 follows this ticket)
- no artifact scoping change and no extractor swap (both ancora-gqb)

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission ends result=pass
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

RULING part 1 of 2 (Manuel, 2026-09-03):
F9: Option A, implement the memo. Thread RunContext into Gate.def_indexes/2 and Derive.resolve_file/4, make memo_put/4 and memo_get/2 real on the parse and DefIndex paths, and prove hits with a counter or trace test (not timing). memo_is_run_scoped stays as written; no ADR. The table is still created per run and deleted at run end. Coordinate with ancora-xla.3, whose F15 re-parse fix now goes through this memo.
F13: Option A, deprecate now and remove in 2.0. Document the spec-exceptions key as deprecated in the parse_file/2 contract, README, and docs/migration.md. Keep parsing it; add nothing to Verifier. Before writing the note, grep the Engage, Builder, and Atlas corpora for an exceptions block and report on this ticket if anything uses it; a live consumer changes the answer.

The gqb-blocks-xla.9 dependency is removed, so this ticket is ready now. Scope here is F9 (implement the memo) and F13 (deprecate spec-exceptions) only.

RULING REVISED (Manuel, 2026-09-03), supersedes part 1 for F9:

Remove the ETS memo half of RunContext (memo_put/4, memo_get/2, the kind-rank arbitration table, and the table create/delete), and the six test assertions in test/ancora/git_test.exs that were its only callers. The batch-port half stays. Narrow ancora.derive.memo_is_run_scoped under a new ADR whose affects: names that requirement id (per the ancora-v1n rule). test/ancora/git_test.exs:149 "run context carries only batch-port state and closes the port" holds the ETS claim on its own evidence, not on the struct it just built. The load-bearing assertion is the pair of refute_received lines at 177-178, backed by :erlang.trace(self(), true, [:call]) plus global trace patterns on {:ets, :new, 2} and {:ets, :delete, 1} installed before RunContext.start/2 runs. Reintroducing an ETS allocation in start/2 fires a {:trace, pid, :call, {:ets, :new, _}} message into the test mailbox and the refute fails, and this holds whether the table is named or unnamed and whether or not it is stored on the struct, which is exactly the mutation the old assertions could not distinguish. Two further assertions kill weaker variants: Map.keys(ctx) |> Enum.sort() == [:__struct__, :base, :batch_port, :root] at 166 kills any new struct field including a plain-map memo, and the two refute function_exported? lines at 167-168 kill a restored public memo API at its old arities. Port.info(ctx.batch_port.port, :registered_name) == {:registered_name, []} at 169 kills registering the port, which is the surviving proof of cross-run isolation now that the two-concurrent-runs test is gone, and Port.info(port) == nil at 174 after stop kills a stop/1 that drops the port on the floor. Verified against lib/ancora/git/batch_port.ex that open/1 only calls System.find_executable/1 and Port.open/2, so nothing on the production path touches ETS and the refutes cannot false-positive. The test does not lean on the module's async: false: the trace flag is set on self() only, so trace delivery is process-scoped and self-isolating; the on_exit at 158-161 clears the two global trace patterns, and it runs before the setup's TmpGitRepo cleanup under LIFO ordering.

test/ancora/parser_test.exs:376 "parse_file/2 is exported and documented as stable" pulls the docs chunk with Code.fetch_docs/1 and asserts on both the moduledoc and the parse_file/2 docstring, so the deprecation statement is proven where the ticket said it must live: on the semver-stable contract itself, not in a comment. The six added assertions at 398-403 kill deleting the deprecation note, dropping the 2.0 removal date, and stating it on only one of the two doc surfaces. Because the source of truth is @doc and @moduledoc rather than a fixture, a rewrite that keeps the promise but changes the wording is the only thing that breaks it, and that is a real contract edit, not a harmless refactor.

test/ancora/parser_test.exs:407 "return shape includes the Atlas contract keys" adds "exceptions" and "findings" to the required-key loop, killing a silent removal of either key from the published 1.x map. Non-blocking observation: the added assert spec["exceptions"] == [] at 416 is fixture reassertion, since @specled_017 carries no spec-exceptions block, so on its own it proves only that the key is present and empty. The stronger claim, that a corpus with an exceptions block still parses in 1.x, is held by the untouched test at test/ancora/parser_test.exs:116 "exceptions block still parses", which asserts [%Exception{id: "with.exception.gap", reason: "accepted gap"}] from a real spec-exceptions block. That test is the actual regression guard for the deprecation-without-removal ruling and it stays green, so the contract is covered; the new line adds little beyond the key-presence loop above it.

Non-blocking observation 2: the README and docs/migration.md deprecation paragraphs are prose-only with no test asserting them, unlike the docstrings. The ticket's Behaviors-to-demonstrate line for F13 names only the parse_file/2 return contract, which is test-backed, so this is not a gap against the stated contract, but the two documents can drift from the docstrings without any test noticing.

Non-blocking observation 3: the ancora.gate.no_derived_state sentence says stopping the run context leaves no table or process behind. The test proves the table half three ways and proves the port is gone, but makes no assertion over the process set, so a memo reintroduced as a supervised Agent rather than an ETS table would evade it. The derive-side sentence this test is tagged to, ancora.derive.memo_is_run_scoped, speaks only about ETS and is fully proven, and the ruling's scope was the ETS memo, so I am not treating this as blocking.
